what_this_is: The amend-only set of THIS repository: the evidence documents (`docs/eval-data/*.md`)
and `docs/eval.md`. A path listed here is judged by the record-vs-pointer rule; a path
not listed here is not judged at all, and amendguard says `unmeasured=1` and exits 3
rather than 0 when the patterns match nothing in the range it was given (RB-P51).
corrected_2026_09_06: This sentence used to end `the evidence documents and the register`, and the register
was NOT in the list below — `docs/roadmap-toolbox.md` has never been in it. The phrase
had no referent: `docs/eval.md` is the eval harness's usage document, not a register,
and `docs/record-vs-pointer.md` never uses the word. So the document the rule was
written for sat outside the gate that enforces it, and the sentence said otherwise.
Found by the review of job44, which had rewritten one register record in place — the
only one of that job's 22 closures to do it — and passed this gate while doing so.

docs/roadmap-toolbox.md: THE REGISTER IS DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS LIST, AND THAT IS A STATED CONTRADICTION
RATHER THAN A RESOLVED ONE. It is the document the record-vs-pointer rule most wants
gated, and adding it here today would be wrong for a measured reason, not a feared
one.
MEASURED 2026-09-06 (job44, unit F4). With `amend_only` set to
`["docs/roadmap-toolbox.md"]` and nothing else:
python tools/amendguard/amendguard.py check . f484c70..c6bfdeb <that ledger>
returns `rows=1 ok=0 red=1`, verdict RECORD-EDITED, naming five hunks `rewritten in
place` at new-file lines 39, 51, 56, 80 and 82. Exactly ONE of the five (line 56) is
the real violation — a follow-up paragraph replaced instead of amended, since
restored. The other four are legitimate amendments that the checker cannot tell
apart from rewrites: line 51 appends a closure to the END of an existing paragraph's
last line, and lines 80 and 82 append closures INTO existing table-row cells, which
is this file's whole convention (a row is one line, so extending a cell is a `replace`
hunk under `classify_hunks`'s line-level difflib). Line 39 is a qualification inserted
mid-sentence, which is a genuine in-place edit of a record and is the borderline case.
So the honest count is: gating the register today would redden roughly four in five of
its legitimate closures, and the file would be edited to please the checker rather than
the checker taught to read the file.
A SECOND, SEPARATE CONSEQUENCE, because `amend_only` is read by more than amendguard:
`runtime-py/tests/test_served_tool_count_records.py` loads this same list and uses it as
an EXEMPT set for its served-tool-count claim scan (`_amend_only`, line 120). Widening
the list therefore also narrows that test's coverage — a second, silent effect that any
future widening has to account for.
THE DESIGN DECISION THIS NEEDS, stated so the next round finds it instead of
re-deriving it. Three candidates, none taken here because each is a change to a layer
this unit does not own:
(1) teach `classify_hunks` a LINE-SUFFIX APPEND class — a `replace` hunk whose new
line has the old line as a strict prefix adds text and destroys none, so it is an
`append`, not a `record`. Smallest change, matches the rule's own reasoning
(`an addition destroys no record`), and would leave line 56 red while greening 51,
80 and 82. It is a change to tools/amendguard/amendguard.py with its own
calibration fixture and mutation-coverage discipline.
(2) change the register's convention so a closure is a NEW line rather than an
extension of an existing one. Correct, and a rewrite of a document whose row 8
cell is 18,424 characters on one line.
(3) leave the register ungated and say so — what is done here.
Registered in docs/roadmap-toolbox.md as (bb).

closed_2026_09_11: THE `not_covered` BLOCK ABOVE IS SUPERSEDED AND IS LEFT VERBATIM. It is a record, so it
is amended here rather than rewritten — the same rule this file gates. Everything it
says was true when it was written; two of its numbers have since been re-measured and
one of its three candidate designs has been REFUTED by running it.
WHAT J46-32 MEASURED. `docs/roadmap-toolbox.md`, `docs/roadmap-agent-stack.md` and
`docs/porting.md` are now in `amend_only`. Over the whole of this branch —
python tools/amendguard/amendguard.py check . 6e506ca..df48b68 tools/amendguard/ledger.json
— 40 commits, 19 rows. Before teaching amendguard anything: `rows=19 ok=11 red=8`, of
which 7 were RECORD-EDITED and 1 was a STAMP-MISSING in `docs/eval-data/` that the
SHIPPED ledger already reported (`rows=3 ok=2 red=1`) and that this widening did not
cause. After the `amendment` class: `rows=19 ok=16 red=3`.
CANDIDATE (1) ABOVE IS REFUTED, BY RUNNING IT. The block proposes a LINE-SUFFIX APPEND —
`a replace hunk whose new line has the old line as a strict prefix`. Applied to the seven
RECORD-EDITED hunks it greens ZERO of them. Not one closure on this branch was written at
the end of its line, because a table row ENDS IN `|`: a closure goes into the last cell,
before that pipe, and a struck row turns `| 12 |` into `| ~~12~~ |` in the middle. The
earlier estimate that four in five legitimate closures would redden was right about the
proportion and wrong about the shape.
WHAT WAS BUILT INSTEAD: `destroys_nothing`, a CHARACTER-level test over the whole hunk —
an edit that only INSERTS characters destroys no record and is an `amendment`. It greens
five of the seven. Calibrated by the pair `AMEND-IN-PLACE` (green) / `AMEND-BUT-DELETES`
(red, one character gone from a line that got far longer), pinned by
`test_a_record_extended_in_place_without_destroying_anything_is_ok` and
`test_an_in_place_extension_that_destroys_one_character_is_still_red`, and swept by
MUT-AMENDMENT and MUT-AMENDMENT-LENGTH-ONLY, both PINNED at flips=0.
THE TWO THAT STAY RED ARE REAL, and they are findings rather than false positives:
* 181744a8 `docs/roadmap-agent-stack.md` line 158 — `fix(records): mark two dated
11-tools observations`. Three lines of a record were replaced by one; 6 characters
destroyed. The intent was to DATE a record and the method was to rewrite it.
* a7f90073 `docs/porting.md` line 250 — two backslashes removed from inside a table
cell (`\`…\`` -> `` `…` ``). 2 characters destroyed, 0 inserted.
Neither can be undone: they are committed history, and history is not amended. They are
recorded here so the next `check` over this range finds an explanation rather than a
mystery.
THE SECOND, SILENT CONSEQUENCE THE BLOCK ABOVE WARNED ABOUT, MEASURED.
`runtime-py/tests/test_served_tool_count_records.py` reads this same `amend_only` list as
an EXEMPT set. Counting its census both ways over the tracked tree: SHIPPED list
`checked=29 exempt_by_ledger=4 exempt_by_marker=19`; WIDENED list `checked=29
exempt_by_ledger=7 exempt_by_marker=16`. Three claims move from marker-exemption to
ledger-exemption and `checked` does not move, so NO live claim loses its check today. A
NEW served-tool claim written into one of the three files would now be blanket-exempt
instead of checked — which is that gate's own stated rule (`those files cannot be edited
in place at all, so EVERY figure in them is dated by construction`) applying to a file
that has just become amend-only, rather than a hole opened for convenience.
